title: AWS S3 and CloudFront Certificate Authority change
content:
Background

AWS announced in 2018 a broad migration to its own Certificate Authority, Amazon Trust Services. AWS purchased the Starfield Services CA to accomplish that.

Since then several services has already moved over to use certificates from Amazon Trust Services, including but not limited to EC2 and DynamoDB.

S3 and CloudFront

In March 2021 the rollout of changing Certificate Authority for DEFAULT certificates for S3 and CloudFront will start. However for S3 this has already happened in the following regions, eu-west-3, eu-north-1, me-south-1, ap-northeast-3, ap-east-1, and us-gov-east-1.

What do I need to do?

You need to ensure that you application will function properly after the change.

Please make sure to do this as soon as possible to avoid any downtime!

CloudFront

If you use your own domain, e.g. example.com and your own certificate for that domain you are not affected by this change. If you use CloudFront default domain and certificate, e.g. https://d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net you must ensure that your application / browser trust the new CA. That can be done with the links on this page https://www.amazontrust.com/repository/

Don’t forget to test on Kiosk browsers as well.

All modern browsers should already be good to go.

S3

The easiest way to test S3 is to create a bucket in the already migrated regions, e.g. eu-north-1. Upload a file to this bucket and then try to download it from the application.

Need help or advise?

If you feel you need help to verify or advise what to do contact the DevOps team (devops@inter.ikea.com)
